spec_review.caveat: the primary xHCI and PCIe specification PDFs could not be retrieved in this environment (one fetch hit an anti-bot page); points below come from secondary sources found by search and from established driver practice, and are labelled accordingly
spec_review.xhci_hcrst: HCRST is cleared by the controller when reset completes; software must not end it early by writing 0 and must not write operational or runtime registers while it is 1; completion is HCRST=0 and USBSTS.CNR=0 (secondary source quoting xHCI 5.4.1)
spec_review.xhci_timeout: no timeout is specified; some controllers need over 100 ms, some need about 1 ms before CNR can be polled (secondary sources: SeaBIOS list, 9front); real-hardware timing is therefore out of scope for QEMU-only evidence and the dry-run defines only an iteration bound
spec_review.pci_bus_master: clearing Bus Master Enable stops a function issuing new memory requests including MSI/MSI-X but does not by itself guarantee that requests already issued have completed; the PCIe Device Status Transactions Pending bit and a flushing read are the usual way to confirm (secondary sources); some hardware has been reported to send MSI regardless
spec_review.order_conclusion: bus-master-first remains acceptable for a halted, idle controller, with three additions adopted in C3b.1: (1) PCIe Transactions Pending must read 0 at every revalidation, (2) USBSTS must remain exactly 1 (HSE clear) after the clear, (3) the proposed read-back is a non-posted config read. Reset-first would also be safe for a halted controller (a completed reset zeroes the pointers) but leaves a window if the reset hangs; bus-master-first closes it.
spec_review.unverified: that HCRST leaves PCI configuration (including BME) untouched is the expected architectural separation but was not confirmed from the specification text
